method: Introspection only, via `busctl --system introspect <name> <path> --xml-interface --no-pager` and `busctl --system list/tree`, parsed with ElementTree. NO D-Bus method was invoked and NO property was read via Properties.Get, with the two disclosed exceptions in the caveats block below. Member counts in this file were computed by XML parse, not by grep, because grep-based counting on QtDBus output (which puts whole interfaces on one line) undercounts.
caveats: Introspecting an unowned but activatable name STARTS the service. org.freedesktop.hostname1, locale1 and timedate1 are activatable and were started by introspection in a prior session; they are unowned again now, so this session did NOT re-introspect them and their shapes below are carried forward from that session with attribution. org.bluez was likewise not re-attempted.

`busctl introspect` without --xml-interface reads property VALUES via org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.GetAll. That non-XML form was used exactly once this session, against org.freedesktop.DBus /org/freedesktop/DBus, to read the daemon's Features and Interfaces properties. It is a read, but it is a method call, and it is disclosed here rather than buried.
The systemd unit-object shapes were introspected on xochitl_2eservice specifically. Path escaping: '.' -> _2e, '-' -> _2d, and a leading digit is hex-escaped.

claims.path_escaping: systemd hex-escapes a leading digit as _3<digit> and '-' as _2d. So /link/_31 = ifindex 1, _33 = 3, _34 = 4, _38 = 8. Network config objects decode: _310_2dusb = "10-usb", _325_2dwlan0 = "25-wlan0", _326_2dbnep0 = "26-bnep0", _342_2dethernet = "42-ethernet", and five stock systemd 80-*.network files (_380_2d6rd_2dtunnel, _380_2dcontainer_2dvb/-ve/-vz, _380_2dvm_2dvt, _380_2dwifi_2dadhoc).

claims.shape: The org.freedesktop.DBus.{Peer,Introspectable,Properties} trio comes in THREE distinguishable flavours on this device, and it is not universally present. You can identify a service's generator from introspection alone.

flavours.sd-bus: GetAll out-arg named "props"; Introspect out-arg "xml_data"; GetMachineId out-arg "machine_uuid"; PropertiesChanged signal args carry NO direction attribute; no annotations. Seen on hostname1, systemd1, login1, network1, resolve1, no.remarkable.marker.
flavours.Qt-annotated: GetAll out-arg named "values" plus org.qtproject.QtDBus.QtTypeName.Out0=QVariantMap; PropertiesChanged signal args carry direction="out" (an sd-bus impossibility) plus QtTypeName.Out1=QVariantMap. Seen on no.remarkable.update1 and no.remarkable.sync.
flavours.Qt-unnamed: out-args carry NO name at all; Get/Set/GetAll declared in that order; Introspect and GetMachineId out-args also unnamed. Seen on com.remarkable.devicepolicy.

claims.shape: com.remarkable.devicepolicy is reachable by ANY local uid. The other three reMarkable services are root-only. Two of the three enforce that with an explicit default deny; marker relies on dbus-daemon's implicit deny.

matrix.com.remarkable.devicepolicy: root may own; <policy context="default"><allow send_destination="com.remarkable.devicepolicy"/></policy> -- ANY local uid may send
matrix.no.remarkable.marker: root-only via <policy user="root">{allow own, allow send_destination}</policy>; NO default stanza, so the implicit deny applies
matrix.no.remarkable.sync: root allow own+send, plus explicit <policy context="default"><deny send_destination="no.remarkable.sync"/></policy>
matrix.no.remarkable.update1: root allow own+send, explicit default deny, plus a dead-code allowlist for uid "core"

claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'cat /usr/share/dbus-1/system.d/com.remarkable.devicepolicy.conf' -> "<policy user=\"root\"><allow own=\"com.remarkable.devicepolicy\"/></policy><policy context=\"default\"><allow send_destination=\"com.remarkable.devicepolicy\"/></policy>"; $ cat .../no.remarkable.marker.conf -> only "<policy user=\"root\"><allow own=\"no.remarkable.marker\"/><allow send_destination=\"no.remarkable.marker\"/></policy>"; $ cat .../no.remarkable.sync.conf -> root allow plus "<policy context=\"default\"><deny send_destination=\"no.remarkable.sync\" /></policy>"; $ cat /etc/dbus-1/system.d/no.remarkable.update1.conf -> root allow, then "<policy user=\"core\">" with "<!-- introspection is denied --><deny ... send_interface=\"org.freedesktop.DBus.Introspectable\" /><deny ... send_interface=\"org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties\" />" and explicit allows for AttemptUpdate, ResetStatus, GetStatus, then "<policy context=\"default\"><deny send_destination=\"no.remarkable.update1\" /></policy>"; $ ssh remarkable 'grep "^core:" /etc/passwd || echo "no core user"' -> "no core user".
claims.notes: Two findings. (1) devicepolicy is the one reMarkable service any unprivileged local process can reach: GetPolicies()/GetEnrolledState() are readable by anyone, and SetPolicyStatus is callable by anyone -- gated by nothing in the bus policy. (2) The update1 "core" stanza is inherited ChromeOS/Flatcar boilerplate that never applies, but its intent is instructive: upstream considered INTROSPECTION itself privileged on this service. Introspection succeeded here only because the session is root.

claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'ls /usr/share/dbus-1/system.d/ /etc/dbus-1/system.d/' -> /etc: "dbus-wpa_supplicant.conf, no.remarkable.update1.conf"; /usr/share: "bluetooth.conf, com.remarkable.devicepolicy.conf, no.remarkable.marker.conf, no.remarkable.sync.conf, org.freedesktop.{hostname1,locale1,login1,network1,resolve1,systemd1,timedate1}.conf"; $ ls /usr/share/dbus-1/system-services/ -> "com.remarkable.devicepolicy.service, no.remarkable.marker.service, org.bluez.service, org.freedesktop.{hostname1,locale1,login1,network1,resolve1,systemd1,timedate1}.service"; $ ls -l /etc/systemd/system/ | grep "^l" | grep dbus -> "dbus-com.remarkable.devicepolicy.service -> /usr/lib/systemd/system/mdm-agent.service / dbus-fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1.service -> .../wpa_supplicant.service / dbus-org.bluez.service -> .../bluetooth.service / dbus-org.freedesktop.network1.service -> .../systemd-networkd.service / dbus-org.freedesktop.resolve1.service -> .../systemd-resolved.service".
claims.notes: no.remarkable.sync and no.remarkable.update1 have policy files but NO activation file -- they are boot-started only and cannot be bus-activated. Conversely fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1 has a policy file and an Alias symlink but no activation file in system-services/.

claims.shape: Introspect on a PARENT path of mdm-agent returns the child's FULL interface definitions nested inside <node name="child">, not merely the child's name. sd-bus and QtDBus both emit only <node name="child"/> stubs.
claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'dbus-send --system --print-reply --dest=com.remarkable.devicepolicy /com/remarkable org.freedesktop.DBus.Introspectable.Introspect' -> a single reply containing "<node>...<node name=\"devicepolicy\"><interface name=\"com.remarkable.devicepolicy.MDMAgent1\"> ...full method and signal list inline... </interface>...</node></node>"; contrast $ busctl --system introspect com.remarkable.devicepolicy /com/remarkable/devicepolicy/bogus -> "Failed to introspect object ...: Unknown object", same for /bogus.
claims.consequence: (a) A single Introspect at /com or /com/remarkable yields the complete devicepolicy API. (b) busctl --xml-interface at a parent path DOUBLE-REPORTS interfaces, which is what initially looked like MDMAgent1 being registered at two paths. (c) The 'Unknown object' replies prove there is no sd-bus fallback prefix, so MDMAgent1 lives at exactly /com/remarkable/devicepolicy.

claims.shape: org.bluez is registered as activatable with its policy installed, but activation blocks for the full 25s service_start_timeout and never yields an owner. Zero object paths obtainable. bluetooth.service is loaded/inactive/dead despite being enabled.

(exit 1). Re-verified this session WITHOUT re-triggering activation: $ busctl --system list -> "org.bluez  pid=-  -  unit=-"; activation and policy files present per the inventory claim above.

claims.shape: Device is UNENROLLED. GetPolicies returns 0 policies. Four policy names are observable from the log: BlockDeveloperMode, BlockRetail, BlockSSH, SoftwareAutoInstall -- all last applied as false.
claims.evidence: read from the /log.txt oracle, not by invoking any method: $ grep -F 'rm.modules.mdm.policymanager' /log.txt -> "Set policy state false on PolicyName::BlockDeveloperMode (operator()<xofm::libs::devicepolicy::PolicyName, std::weak_ptr<xofm::libs::devicepolicy::IPolicy> > /home/runner/work/xochitl/xochitl/src/xofm/modules/devicepolicy/devicepolicymanager.cpp:110)", same for PolicyName::BlockRetail, PolicyName::BlockSSH, PolicyName::SoftwareAutoInstall; $ grep -F 'rm.modules.mdm.dbus.policyagent' /log.txt -> "GetPolicies returned 0 policies (getPolicies .../src/xofm/modules/mdm/policyagent.cpp:57)".
claims.consequence: BlockSSH=false plus an empty policy set is one of the two independent reasons SSH is reachable (the other being secboot=unlocked gating dropbear@.service). Note that empty-policy-set, not an explicit allow, is why BlockSSH reads false.

refuted.claim: The sd-bus flavour of the standard trio is present on all 20+ objects enumerated, and only two flavour variants exist on the device.
refuted.observation: Both universals fail. fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1 is a THIRD shape: in-args named "interface"/"propname" (not interface_name/property_name), Introspect out-arg "data" (not xml_data), NO PropertiesChanged signal on the Properties interface, and NO org.freedesktop.DBus.Peer interface at all -- re-verified this session by ElementTree parse: "org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties  M=3 S=0 P=0" and no Peer entry. And com.remarkable.devicepolicy is a fourth: every out-arg is UNNAMED, including GetMachineId and Introspect. Container paths can carry zero interfaces: /fi introspects to "<node><node name=\"w1\"/></node>".
refuted.correction: Three flavours plus a presence caveat. See claim standard-interface:three-flavours.

refuted.claim: org.freedesktop.login1.Manager has 55 methods / 9 signals / 47 properties, of which 2 are readwrite and 45 are read.
refuted.observation: Signals are right; methods and properties are not. ElementTree parse of the same object: "org.freedesktop.login1.Manager  M=59 S=9 P=46 ro=44 rw=2". Independent grep over the Manager interface block agrees (59/9/46, 2 readwrite, 44 read), as does the tabular busctl form. The claim's own shape field in fact enumerates all 59 method names while labelling the group "(55)", and 2+45=47 is one phantom read property.
refuted.correction: 59 methods / 9 signals / 46 properties (44 read + 2 readwrite: EnableWallMessages, WallMessage). Every member name, signature, annotation and the owner pid 370 verified exact.

refuted.claim: org.freedesktop.network1.DHCPv4Client and .DHCPv6Client are present on every /link/_XX object.
refuted.observation: Neither is. Interface sets measured this session: /link/_31 (lo) and /link/_33 (usb0) carry ONLY org.freedesktop.network1.Link; /link/_34 (usb1) carries DHCPv6Client and DHCPServer but NOT DHCPv4Client; only the wlan0 object carries DHCPv4Client. networkd instantiates these per-link, conditional on what is actually configured -- usb1 SERVES DHCP (hence DHCPServer) rather than consuming it.
refuted.correction: The interface set on a link object is conditional, not a uniform schema. usb1 additionally exports org.freedesktop.network1.DHCPServer, which no prior claim recorded.

refuted.observation: /link/_36 no longer exists: $ busctl --system introspect org.freedesktop.network1 /org/freedesktop/network1/link/_36 -> "Unknown object '/org/freedesktop/network1/link/_36'." wlan0's ifindex is now 8, and the object is /link/_38. $ ssh remarkable 'for d in /sys/class/net/*; do printf "%s=" "$(basename $d)"; cat $d/ifindex; done' -> "lo=1 usb0=3 usb1=4 wlan0=8". The link tree lists _31, _33, _34, _38.
refuted.correction: Only the ESCAPING RULE is firmware-invariant (leading digit hex-escaped, so _3<n> = ifindex n, and _2d = '-'). The specific numbers track live ifindex, which increments across wifi interface teardown/recreate. A client must resolve link paths by reading /sys/class/net/*/ifindex at runtime, never by hard-coding _36.

refuted.claim: LogControl1's LogLevel and LogTarget are the ONLY genuinely writable D-Bus properties anywhere on the device; everything else that mutates is a method.
refuted.observation: False by a wide margin. ElementTree parse this session: org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager has 8 readwrite properties, six of which have nothing to do with logging -- RuntimeWatchdogUSec, RuntimeWatchdogPreUSec, RuntimeWatchdogPreGovernor, RebootWatchdogUSec, KExecWatchdogUSec, ServiceWatchdogs. org.freedesktop.login1.Manager has 2 (EnableWallMessages, WallMessage). fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1 has 3 (DebugLevel, DebugTimestamp, DebugShowKeys), its Interfaces/0 object has 108 across two interfaces, and Network objects add Enabled and Properties.
refuted.correction: The LogControl1 shape and its 7-present/4-absent distribution are exact; the exclusivity note is not. wpa_supplicant's DebugLevel is a second bus-tunable log knob outside LogControl1, and DebugShowKeys would leak PSKs into the /log.txt oracle.

refuted.claim: com.remarkable.devicepolicy's activation file points at a nonexistent unit (SystemdService=dbus-com.remarkable.devicepolicy.service), a latent packaging bug that would fall through to Exec=/bin/false.
refuted.observation: The unit exists. $ ssh remarkable 'ls -l /etc/systemd/system/ | grep "^l" | grep dbus' -> "dbus-com.remarkable.devicepolicy.service -> /usr/lib/systemd/system/mdm-agent.service" -- the standard systemd Alias symlink, in the HIGHEST-precedence unit directory, installed from mdm-agent.service's [Install] Alias=. Four sibling names use the identical idiom (bluez, wpa_supplicant, network1, resolve1). The original probe checked only /lib/systemd/system, the VENDOR dir, where Alias symlinks are never written (and /lib is itself a symlink to usr/lib).
refuted.correction: No packaging bug. Activation resolves to mdm-agent.service and restarts it; Exec=/bin/false is never reached. The sub-claim that no.remarkable.sync and no.remarkable.update1 lack activation files entirely DOES hold.

refuted.observation: ElementTree parse this session: "fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1.Interface  M=37 S=19 P=122 ro=22 rw=100". The claim is also internally inconsistent: it enumerates exactly 22 read-only names, so "everything else" of 149 would be 127, not ~110.
refuted.correction: 122 properties: 22 read, 100 readwrite, 0 write-only. All 37 method and 19 signal signatures verified exact. The directional point survives -- 100 writable properties on one object versus 2 across all of logind.
